put.description:
Renames the unit, assigns its manager, reassigns it or takes the manager off it. Taking off is how two
managers change places, since neither can be given a unit while holding one.

post.description:
The unit lets its manager go, who can then hold another. There is no way back: a hospital that reopens a
unit creates one under the name, which is free again, and the old one stays on record.

put.description:
Saving is the review: it clears the flag even when nothing else changed. Under the catalogue's lock, so that a
code the CNO is retiring or renaming at this moment cannot be written.

put.description:
A manager with a nurse profile sets their own, because nobody else may and a nurse has to have them. The CNO and the
Deputy CNO can read the values, and the log shows whose hand changed them. Ticket 21 refuses the opening values here
once the nurse's first month has closed.

All a manager can change of a nurse due to join: a unit may roster a month ahead of their arrival, and this list is
about this unit's shifts, whereas the rest is about the nurse and stays with the manager of the unit they are in.

The active unit managers with no nurse profile yet.

post.description: The role and the account stay as they are, so no password here. Their hospital ID is the username they have.

put.description:
A staff nurse's account follows: today or earlier deactivates at once, because ending an account should not
wait, a later date when it has passed (`nurses.tasks`), and clearing it or moving it on brings them back. A
manager's account is the System Admin's, so their profile ends alone.

Nothing here changes who belongs where, now or to come, nor an account's state, so no unit's row is locked and
an ended nurse stays ended. Ticket 21 adds the guard for a closed month here, and ticket 11 warns of a solved one.

post.description:
A staff nurse's only: a manager's account is the System Admin's, and this would let one bypass their own
current password. A manager reaches the nurses of their unit this month, and the same 403 otherwise.
Every row's problems. It saves nothing and keeps nothing: confirming sends the file again.

`token` is the preview's. The file is judged again from the start: with any problem, or when it no longer means
what was previewed, nothing is saved and the answer is 409 with the preview as it now stands.

nurse too, and one holding no unit has no other way to read theirs; one with no profile simply has none. Days left
outside the nurse's dates by a later correction are not here: they count for nothing, and are their manager's to clear.
